answer.location_description: Small patch at the left image edge, roughly rows 7-9 and columns 0-2, around pixel (8,2), well outside the central blob area.
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright patch / edge pixel cluster
answer.mechanism: Layer 1 has two families of units. The 'ring/large-blob' units (0, 1, 8, 18, 19, 20, 22, 29) have positive weights on an annulus around the centre. The 'small-blob/background' units (14, 15, 23, 27) have a positive centre, a negative ring and positive weights on the periphery. In the left-edge patch the background units carry unusually large positive weights (up to +99) and the ring units carry large negative weights (down to -84). Brightness there therefore excites units 14/15/23/27 and suppresses the ring units. Layer 2 routes this toward class 0: units 23 and 27 feed negatively into the positively weighted layer-2 units u3, u10 and u14. Units 14, 15, 23 and 27 feed positively into the negatively weighted layer-2 units u1 and u6.
answer.evidence: Pixel (8,2) is the strongest weight in the whole layer: 99 (unit 14), 88 (unit 15), 86 (unit 23), 79 (unit 27), versus -84 (unit 1), -78 (unit 19), -76 (unit 29), -70 (unit 22), -57 (unit 18). Nearby pixels follow the same opposite-sign pattern. At (8,0), (9,0) and (7,0) the background units sit at about 53-77 and the ring units at about -27 to -53. The mirror region at the right edge (rows 7-9, cols 21-23) shows no such pattern. The cluster is far from the blob, where size information should not live. One exception: (7,1) has the reversed sign, so the patch may be textured rather than uniform. Other strong sign-consistent pixels are scattered elsewhere, e.g. (1,16-17), (3,5), (3,12) and (16,21). This makes the patch identification only moderately certain.
answer.main_feature: Radial size template: ring units respond to brightness in an annulus at radius about 4-7 around the centre (signalling a large blob). Units 14/15/23/27 respond to a bright centre with a dark surrounding ring (signalling a small blob). Layer 2 contrasts the two families.
